items.title: Sam Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: I did a little 45 with Dick Hyman and Clyde Lombardi, and Jackie Moffett I think.

ctx.x: When was the first opportunity to record for you?

Let me see when was the first. I had a friend, his name was Arnold Rosen and he was kind of like a pusher you know. He pushed me because he thought I was the next Benny Goodman you know, at the time. And so I think he might have been influential. I reckon the first one had Dick Hyman on piano. This is, I’m not sure, in 1952 or whatever it was, I did a little 45 with Dick Hyman and Clyde Lombardi, and Jackie Moffett I think. This was the personnel. That was a 45. That’s when 45s were around. And if I’m not…
